questions.q: Where will your streaming system run?
questions.hint: Think about where your apps live today, and where they might live in three years.

options.label: On AWS, and we plan to stay
On AWS now, maybe elsewhere later
options.why: you may leave AWS and want portable client code

options.label: Several clouds or our own data centres
options.why: you need something that runs outside AWS

questions.hint: Free software still has a bill: servers and people.

options.label: Nobody on my team
options.why: you want the cloud provider to run it

options.label: A vendor runs it, but I choose sizes
options.why: you want a managed service with some control

options.label: We are happy to run it ourselves
options.why: your team can operate a cluster

questions.q: What do you have or need beyond the basics?

options.label: Kafka clients or Kafka connectors
options.why: you already have Kafka code and tools

options.label: Nothing yet, we are starting fresh
options.why: you have no client code to carry over

options.label: Built-in tenants and cross-region copies
options.why: you want multi-tenancy and geo-replication in the platform

questions.q: How long must events stay replayable?

options.label: More than a year
options.why: AWS lists 365 days as the longest Kinesis retention

questions.q: How do you feel about licences?

options.label: A proprietary AWS service is fine
Source-available is fine if it works well
options.why: you can live with the Business Source License

kinesis.name: Kinesis Data Streams
kinesis.summary: AWS's own streaming service, with on-demand or shard-based capacity.
kinesis.bestWhen: you are all-in on AWS and want the least to run.
kinesis.watchOut: it uses AWS's own API, runs only on AWS and keeps data for 365 days at most.

msk.name: Amazon MSK
msk.summary: Apache Kafka run by AWS, in Standard, Express or Serverless form.
msk.bestWhen: you want Kafka's API and tools without running brokers.
msk.watchOut: you still pick brokers unless you use Serverless, which has its own caps and needs IAM access control.

kafka.name: Apache Kafka, self-run
kafka.summary: The open-source original, under the Apache-2.0 licence, on any cloud.
kafka.bestWhen: you run outside AWS or want new releases as they ship.
kafka.watchOut: your team runs, patches and monitors the cluster.

pulsar.name: Apache Pulsar
pulsar.summary: Open source, with stateless brokers, separate storage and built-in geo-replication.
pulsar.bestWhen: multi-tenancy or cross-region copies are the main need.
pulsar.watchOut: the docs we read do not state Kafka API support, so check before reusing Kafka clients.

redpanda.name: Redpanda
redpanda.summary: A streaming platform that speaks the Kafka API from a single binary.
redpanda.bestWhen: you want Kafka's API with a different engine and a vendor-run option.
redpanda.watchOut: the Community Edition is source-available, and Iceberg Topics need an enterprise licence.
